clean_repro.probe: POST /collections/test_mustnot/points/query with filter={'must_not': {'key': 'tag', 'match': {'value': 'x'}}} (single object, not array)
clean_repro.observed: API returns HTTP 200 with result.points=[id=2], correctly excluding tag=x points. Single-object format works identically to array format.

verified_assumptions: Raw request uses single-object format for must_not filter instead of array format
API accepts both formats and processes them identically
Returned result correctly excludes points matching tag=x

contract_grounding.note: No explicit constraint in structured_contract.json requires must/must_not/should to be arrays only. Contract is silent on this parameter format.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: Filter.must_not field uses serde(with='MaybeOneOrMany') deserializer → MaybeOneOrMany::deserialize accepts unit (null), seq (array), and map (single object) via UntaggedEnumVisitor → All three forms normalize to Option<Vec<Condition>> → No validation rejects single-object form
source_grounding.note: Source code implements intentional lenient parsing via MaybeOneOrMany utility. The deserializer explicitly accepts three forms: null (unit), array (seq), and single object (map). This is not a missing validation—it's designed flexibility.

falsification.probe: Test all three forms (null, single-object, array) produce identical behavior
falsification.observed:
1. Single-object: filter={'must_not': {'key': 'tag', 'match': {'value': 'x'}}} → returns [id=2] (excludes tag=x)
2. Array format: filter={'must_not': [{'key': 'tag', 'match': {'value': 'x'}}]} → returns [id=2] (identical result)
3. Null: filter={'must_not': null} → returns [id=1, id=2] (no filtering)
All forms work correctly with no semantic difference.
falsification.evidence_cmd: curl -s -X POST 'http://localhost:6333/collections/test_mustnot/points/query' -d '{"query": [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4], "filter": {"must_not": null}}' returns all points; other forms return filtered results correctly.

mundane_explanation.note: This is intentional API design for backward compatibility and user convenience, not a bug.

cognition_match.developer_quote: Lenient filter parsing: null / single-object / array forms are all accepted by design for filter condition fields (maintainers: 'This is fine and expected... it would be a breaking change'; source supports all three forms)

contract.explicit_requirement: None - contract is silent on whether must/must_not/should must be arrays
contract.note: No constraint requiring strict array-only format exists in structured_contract.json

physical.objective_constraint: None - no physical or semantic constraint prohibits single-object filter form
physical.note: No objective law of nature that filter arrays cannot be single objects

behavioral.note: API handles all three forms (null/single-object/array) gracefully via MaybeOneOrMany deserializer. Source shows this is intentional design, not an oversight.

perspective_analysis.aggregation_applied: verdict_A=NEUTRAL, verdict_B=NEUTRAL, verdict_C=REFUTED(by_design in source) → final=REFUTED

verdicts.rationale: Candidate claims that POST /points/query with filter={'must_not': {single object}} is 'param_validation' defect because must_not 'should be array not single object'. Investigation reveals: (1) Clean repro: API accepts both single-object and array formats identically, returning correct results. (2) Assumption audit: The implicit premise that 'filter conditions must be arrays' is not a documented requirement. (3) Contract grounding: structured_contract.json has no constraint requiring array-only format for must/must_not/should. (4) Source grounding: lib/segment/src/common/utils.rs and types.rs show MaybeOneOrMany deserializer explicitly accepts three forms (null/unit, array/seq, single-object/map) via UntaggedEnumVisitor. This is intentional lenient parsing for backward compatibility. (5) Falsification: Tested all three forms (null, single-object, array) — all produce semantically identical correct behavior. (6) Mundane explanation: developer_cognition.json explicitly lists 'Lenient filter parsing: null / single-object / array forms are all accepted by design' as a by_design pattern. Maintainers state 'This is fine and expected... it would be a breaking change'. Source code confirms this is designed flexibility via MaybeOneOrMany utility, not missing validation. Verdict: FALSE_POSITIVE, root_cause=mundane_api_semantics (by-design lenient filter parsing).
